answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a bridge as the anchor of the cost.
